title: Reservoir Support Sets the Minimum Loss for Non-Hermitian Dynamics
abstract: The minimum loss required to reproduce non-Hermitian dynamics depends on how many physical modes each reservoir can address coherently. Established positive-matrix criteria bound this cost. We construct a phase-controlled cubic-root Su-Schrieffer-Heeger chain in which three-mode reservoirs attain the unrestricted passivity threshold throughout its phase diagram and halve the minimum pair-supported loss at a tuned point. The bound constrains exact conditional trajectories, including time-dependent Markov controls, rather than preparation of one final state. A connected-chain protocol tests effective reservoir support through calibrated finite-time emission. Full system-auxiliary propagation then bounds conditional fidelity and target yield for every one-particle input. A coherent controller that accurately prepares the selected endpoint fails this propagator test. A singular-value bound excludes every unitary realization of the same conditional map. These results connect local reservoir access to a measurable loss cost for prescribed dynamics.
summary: This paper investigates the minimum unavoidable loss when simulating non-Hermitian quantum dynamics using reservoirs with limited physical mode access. By constructing a specific SSH chain, the authors prove that increasing the reservoir's accessible modes significantly lowers the theoretical loss bound, achieving a 50% reduction compared to simpler pair-supported models. This connects local reservoir engineering directly to measurable constraints on quantum process fidelity.
main_problem: The research aims to determine the minimum loss cost required to accurately reproduce complex non-Hermitian quantum dynamics when the system is coupled to a finite-mode reservoir.
main_result: The authors demonstrate that increasing the number of accessible physical modes in the reservoir (e.g., from pair-supported to three-mode) can reduce the minimum required loss bound by up to 50%.
method: The analysis employs established positive-matrix criteria and constructs a phase-controlled Su-Schrieffer-Heeger chain to test the theoretical loss bounds against measurable quantities like conditional fidelity and target yield.
model_or_system: The system involves non-Hermitian lattices exhibiting directional transport and exceptional dynamics, modeled using a no-jump generator $K = H -iM/2$. The dynamics are studied via reservoir coupling and finite-time emission protocols.
key_observables: Loss Cost, Conditional Fidelity ($F_{	ext{cond}}$), Target Yield ($Y$), and the ratio of yields ($Y_3/Y_2$).
important_parameters: The comparison is drawn between pair-supported ($\Gamma_2$) and three-mode ($\Gamma_3$) reservoir supports; the reduction factor approaches 50% with cycle-phase control.
main_assumptions: The analysis involves comparing the bound derived from pair-supported matrices versus those achievable with three-mode reservoirs, and it distinguishes between reproducing dynamics versus preparing a single final state.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the saturation of the support-cost bound, showing the 50% limit achieved by three-mode reservoirs. Figure 2 demonstrates support certification and target yield measurements on a connected chain.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the theoretical framework by defining the loss cost based on reservoir support, constructs a specific physical model (cubic-root SSH chain) to test the bounds, and then uses advanced propagation tests (like finite-time emission and propagator comparisons) to quantify the achievable loss reduction.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the fundamental limitations imposed by realistic, finite-dimensional coupling environments (reservoirs) on the ability to simulate or control complex non-Hermitian quantum evolution, which is crucial for understanding open quantum systems.

The bounds have 99% simultaneous coverage over all 5120 binomial groups, conditional on the stated calibration bounds.
